text: Circulus in Probando [Lat.]: Ger. Cirkelbeweis ; Fr. (Lat. form), cercle vicieux ; Ital. circolo vizioso . Otherwise called circular reasoning , or argumentin a circle ; a form of the Fallacy of Petitio Principii , generally exhibited in a chain of consecutive reasonings, and consisting in the use as a premise of either the final conclusion to be established or of a proposition which is logically dependent for justification on that conclusion. Literature : WHATELY, Logic, Bk. III. § 13; MILL, Logic, Bk. V. chap. vii. § 2. ( R.A. )
